table.brief: 表头远长于数据：每列表头 8–14 个汉字，数据只有 1–4 个字符的数字或“是/否”

understanding.purpose: A zh-CN server security-baseline audit record: one row per server, one column per control or measure, used to verify compliance and compare servers.
understanding.reading: Readers identify a server in column 1, then scan across its row for pass/fail and counts; auditors also scan down individual check columns to compare servers. Headers are long and can wrap, while row IDs and values are short and must remain stable.
groups: col 1 — server identity / row header; it should stand apart from the checks
cols 2, 3, 5, 8 — binary compliance or confirmation checks (是/否); same visual role
cols 4, 6, 7 — quantitative measures (days, port count, alert count); short numeric values
keep_intact: numeric values such as 180, 365, 30, and port/alert counts
numbers and identifiers must not break across lines
may_wrap: Chinese header labels in every column, especially 受检服务器唯一编号 and 应急联系人确认情况
header text may wrap at character boundaries; no data cell needs wrapping

preferred.name: r0A
preferred.note: Balanced grid: near-equal interior check columns with slightly wider row-ID and contact columns so every header wraps cleanly to two lines.

acceptable.name: r0B
acceptable.note: Status-first: spend width on the four binary checks, keep the three numeric measures at the two-line minimum, and use a compact row-ID column.

acceptable.name: r0C
acceptable.note: Bookend-heavy: make server ID and contact the widest columns while all six check columns sit at the practical two-line minimum.

bad.name: contrast
bad.note: Over-allocates the two edge columns while squeezing all six interior columns to 70px; their 8-character headers fall into three cramped lines, the header rhythm becomes inconsistent, and large empty areas appear in columns 1 and 8. It is plausible as a misguided attempt to favor the row identifier and final contact column, but it damages scanability and proportion.
bad.why: Over-allocates the two edge columns while squeezing all six interior columns to 70px; their 8-character headers fall into three cramped lines, the header rhythm becomes inconsistent, and large empty areas appear in columns 1 and 8. It is plausible as a misguided attempt to favor the row identifier and final contact column, but it damages scanability and proportion.

rationale: r0A is the only design that keeps every header to two lines while leaving all body cells on one line, producing a compact 36px body rhythm and a 60px header. Its wider first and last columns are justified by the 9-character headers, while the six interior columns share a consistent 85px measure. r0B and r0C remain readable and avoid mid-word splits, but their three-line headers add height and create a choppier header band without improving the data cells. The result is a clear hierarchy: identifier column, six comparable status columns, then the contact-confirmation column.

general: In dense tables, set column widths from header phrase breaks and body-cell needs rather than forcing equal widths; a two-line header is usually preferable to a three-line one.
Keep comparable columns at a shared measure so readers can scan across them, but allow edge columns with longer labels to be wider when that prevents extra header lines.
Preserve one-line body cells where possible; row height should be driven by headers, not by avoidable wrapping in short values.
specific: All eight headers here are 8–9 Chinese characters, so roughly 83–97px interior columns and 98–112px edge columns yield two-line headers without mid-word splits.
The first column contains only short IDs, so its extra width is justified by its long header rather than by its data; the same applies to the final contact-confirmation column.
The six middle columns are directly comparable status fields and should stay close to equal width to maintain a consistent scanning rhythm.

tradeoffs: A careful designer might prefer r0C's wider first column because it makes the row identifier header read more comfortably, or r0B's more even distribution, accepting three-line headers in exchange. r0A's edge columns are wider than its numeric content needs, but that is a deliberate trade to keep the header band compact and consistent.
uncertain: The exact wrapping thresholds depend on Chinese glyph advance widths and browser rounding, so the ranges are approximate. Reasonable designers could also accept three-line headers in a publication context where a more even column rhythm matters more than vertical compactness.

critique.good: All eight headers resolve to exactly two lines. The 110px first column gives a clean 5+4 split and visually separates the server IDs as row headers; the six middle columns at 85px give regular 4+4 header splits; the 99px last column gives 5+4. The 60px header and 36px body rows make a compact, even grid that supports both row scanning and column comparison.
critique.problems: No material visual defect. The IDs have spare space, but that is appropriate for a row-header column. The 1px unused width and the slight c1/c8 difference from the middle columns are harmless.
critique.cause: The widths sit at safe two-line thresholds: c1 at 110px has 89px of content, just under the 90px that would trigger an unbalanced 6+3 split; c2–c7 at 85px have 64px, comfortably holding four Chinese characters; c8 at 99px has 78px, holding five. The total is 719px.

critique.good: The wider c2, c3 and c5 columns (100/100/99px) give those headers comfortable two-line breaks, and all body values remain clean and unbroken.
critique.problems: The header row is 83px because c1, c4, c6, c7 and c8 wrap to three lines. Some headers are two lines and others three, so the header block has uneven line counts and wasted vertical space. The first column, which identifies each row, is cramped into three lines, weakening the row-header hierarchy.
critique.cause: c1 at 96px has only 75px of content, just short of the five-character line needed by the bold nine-character header, so it breaks into three lines. c4, c6 and c7 at 81px have 60px of content, only just enough for four characters, so their eight-character headers also break into three lines. c8 at 81px is likewise too narrow. The generous 100px allocations to c2/c3/c5 force the other columns down to 81px.

critique.good: The 103px c8 column keeps the long confirmation header to two lines, and the body values remain clean. The total width is fully used.
critique.problems: The 130px first column is over-wide: its header breaks 7+2, and the two-digit server IDs sit in a very wide column that over-dominates the table. The six middle columns at 81px wrap to three lines, producing an 83px header row with uneven line counts. The result is taller and less balanced than r0A.
critique.cause: c1 at 130px has 109px of content, enough for seven characters on the first line, creating the unbalanced 7+2 split. c8 at 103px also consumes width. The remaining six columns get only 81px (60px of content), so their bold eight-character headers break to three lines.

review.method: two fresh-context blind reviews; letters shuffled; includes browser auto layout and equal widths as neutral references

r0C.why: All eight columns are given nearly the same width, so the 2-character 是/否 and small-number cells sit in wide, airy boxes while the 8-character headers are crushed into three lines that break mid-compound (日志留/存天数/达标, 漏洞补/丁更新/状态, 高危端/口关闭/数量). Legible and uniform, but the width budget is spent where the content is shortest.

r0A.why: Best balance: the row-header column is wide enough for 受检服务器/唯一编号 in two lines, and every other header wraps once at a natural boundary (系统账户/口令强度, 日志留存/天数达标, 应急联系人/确认情况). All body cells stay on one line, header block has a single consistent two-line rhythm, and no column looks starved or padded.

r0B.why: The two identifying columns (first and last) are squeezed to three lines with breaks that split 服务器 and 联系人 (受检服/务器唯/一编号, 应急联/系人确/认情况), while the middle columns get two clean lines. The header block reads ragged and the columns a reader uses to anchor a row are the hardest to parse.

ref_auto.why: Middle columns break cleanly in two lines, but the first and last columns are again compressed to three lines, and the last header ends with a one-character orphan 况 (应急联系/人确认情/况). Reasonable overall rhythm, marred by the two structural columns being the least readable.

ref_equal.why: Six of eight headers break once at a sensible boundary; only the row-header column and the last column drop to three lines, and the last column's break (应急联/系人确/认情况) avoids an orphan. Fairly even rhythm, though the identifier column still deserves more width than the data columns.

contrast.why: The 应急联系人确认情况 column is given roughly twice the width of its neighbours so it fits on a single line, while the six middle headers are crushed into three lines with awkward breaks. The proportions contradict the content: the least dense column is the widest, the header-heavy ones the narrowest.

raw.unsure: Exact pixel widths are hard to measure from the scaled renders, so D and E are close and could swap; also none of the layouts visibly narrows the two small-number columns (高危端口关闭数量, 近三十天告警次数) to buy room for the header-heavy ones, which would be the obvious further refinement on top of B.

r0B.why: Every column is squeezed to roughly the same narrow width, so four headers (col 1, 4, 7, 8) fall to three lines and break words badly — 受检服务|器唯一编|号, 应急联|系人确|认情况. The table also stops ~30px short of the dashed box, so width that could have relieved the wrapping is simply left unused; the data cells themselves stay clean and readable.

ref_auto.why: Fills the full 720px and keeps the six middle headers on two clean lines (系统账户/口令强度, 漏洞补丁/更新状态), so scanning across a row is easy. Weak spot is the hierarchy: the row-identifier column is the narrowest, forcing 受检服务/器唯一编/号 into three lines and splitting 编号, and the last column splits 情况 — the two columns a reader anchors on are the ones that look cramped.

r0C.why: Col 1 and col 8 are given generous width while the six middle columns are crushed to three lines each, and those wraps cut words in half: 系统账|户口令|强度, 外部网|络访问|开放, 漏洞补|丁更新|状态, 高危端|口关闭|数量. The header band becomes tall and hard to parse, and the cramped middle columns are exactly where the comparison data lives.

contrast.why: Same crushed middle columns as C with the same broken words (账|户, 补|丁, 端|口), plus an extreme imbalance: the last header 应急联系人确认情况 sits on one very wide single line while the other seven columns wrap to two or three lines. The eye is pulled to the emptiest column instead of the identifiers and data.

r0A.why: All eight headers resolve to exactly two lines with clean semantic breaks — 受检服务器/唯一编号, 日志留存/天数达标, 应急联系人/确认情况 — no word is split. The first and last columns get slightly more width than the six value columns, matching their roles (row key, confirmation note), the table fills the 720px, and the even two-line header band gives a steady rhythm for row-by-row scanning.

ref_equal.why: Nearly the same distribution as B: middle headers on two lines, but the first and last columns still wrap to three lines splitting 编号 and 情况, and the middle header cells look tighter against the dividers than in B, so the header band feels cramped rather than composed.

raw.unsure: I estimated column widths visually; B and F are very close (possibly identical widths with only a small shift), and I could not verify precisely how much width A leaves unused at the right edge.

provenance.note: AI visual design judgement; not a human reading study
